title: VST: small, staged long into the Q4 catalyst cluster; ~9% to a $150.54 target on 2027 EBITDA roll-forward, not re-rating
call_reason: Target $150.54 is above the $138.02 price with medium conviction and no special situation, but the edge is thin (P(gain) 0.57) so size is capped at 5 shares and entry is staged around the Q3 guide.
one_liner: At ~9x pro-forma 2027 EBITDA of ~$8.15B, VST is priced for the contracted nuclear/PJM book with no credit for ERCOT recovery; formalizing the 2027 guide and a cap-level PJM auction should carry it to ~$151 research target (12m). The Street at ~$219 is paying for an 11x re-rating we don't underwrite, and the stock sits only ~$33 above the $105 thesis-break level at 45-49% vol, so we buy small and add on the print.

thesis.point: 2027 EBITDA of ~$8.1B is largely locked: the low end of the $7.4-7.8B opportunity plus ~$0.7B from Cogentrix and the Meta premium, with 2027 ~94% hedged.
thesis.evidence: CFO on the Q2 call: 2027 'trending towards the lower end' and Cogentrix plus Meta 'add roughly $700 million'; hedges 100%/94%/72% for 2026/27/28. EIA's September STEO held 2027 ERCOT generation at ~527 TWh and raised 2027 ERCOT North to $34.30/MWh, so the August load-growth cut did not extend.

thesis.point: At ~$138 the stock trades at ~9x forward EBITDA, only ~1.8 turns above the 7.25x plain gas-fleet M&A mark, so the contracted nuclear (Meta 2.6 GW PJM, AWS 1.2 GW Comanche Peak) and PJM capacity at the $325 cap are cheaply valued.
thesis.evidence: Cogentrix bought at 7.25x 2027 EBITDA; PJM 2028/29 BRA cleared at the $325/MW-day cap (10,924 MW for Vistra) and the collar extends through 2029/30; ~$23.5B net debt plus preferred and ~337M diluted shares give ~$105 at 7.2x.

thesis.point: Insiders and the balance sheet are supportive: the CEO bought in the open market after the drawdown, and the preferred is being refinanced into cheaper junior notes rather than equity.
thesis.evidence: CEO Form 4 purchases Aug 24 and Aug 31-Sep 1, 2026; $1.5B 7.000%/7.250% junior subordinated notes (Sep 24) fund redemption of the 8.0% Series A and 7.0% Series B preferred at their resets. Offset: the CFO sold 20,000 shares at $151.03 under a 10b5-1 plan.

variant_view: Versus the Street we are the bear: our $150.54 target is ~31% below the weighted analyst median of $218.97 (17 analysts, low $169 Mizuho, high $298). Street targets need ~11x EBITDA or ~$8.5B+ 2028 EBITDA, which requires ERCOT forwards to turn and new hyperscaler deals; with ~28% of 2028 unhedged into a curve still falling in late September, we don't underwrite that. Versus the options market we are only modestly more constructive: the market-implied median is $141.57 with P(gain) 0.52, against our $150.54 and 0.57; our edge is the belief that the Q3 guide formalizes ~$8.1B and that the EIA Texas load cut is already in the price. That is a small variant view, not a big one, and it is why the position is small.

valuation.methods: Supervisor blend, same as the five agents' mean ($150.9; range $145-156): (1) 9.0x ~$8.15B forward EBITDA = ~$73.4B EV, less ~$23.5B net debt plus preferred, over 337M diluted shares = ~$148 (50% weight); (2) ~$13.9/share FCF before growth at a 9% yield = ~$154 (30%); (3) ~13.5x ~$11.1 forward EPS = ~$150 (20%). Blend ~$151. The published 12-month target ($150.54) is the median of the combined options-market and agent distribution; expected value is $170.65 because of the fat right tail (q75 $206.50). Each 0.25x on the multiple is ~$6/share; the $8.1B vs $8.25B EBITDA dispute is ~$2.7/share.

catalysts.event: PJM Reliability Backstop Procurement bid window (~6.8 GW shortfall, cost cap $555/MW-day)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Clearing prices near the cap would confirm scarcity value in PJM and data-center-paid capacity; a weak outcome or political cost-allocation fights would pressure the PJM story ahead of the BRA.
catalysts.watch: Procured MW vs the 6,831 MW target and the clearing price relative to $325 and $555/MW-day.

catalysts.event: Series A preferred first reset / earliest redemption date (8.0% rate ends); Series B reset in Dec 2026
catalysts.why_it_moves: Redemption funded by the Sep-24 junior notes removes the reset risk and lowers the fixed charge; mostly housekeeping.
catalysts.watch: Redemption notice/8-K for the full $1.0B Series A; no equity issuance.

catalysts.why_it_moves: IPP multiples compressed as the 10-year approached 5%; VST is a levered, high-multiple name, so a hawkish surprise hits it harder than the market.
catalysts.watch: Hike vs hold and the 10-year's reaction; a move back above 5% is a multiple headwind.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 earnings and formal 2026/2027 guidance update including Cogentrix and Meta
catalysts.why_it_moves: This is the event that formalizes (or breaks) the ~$8.1B 2027 base the whole valuation sits on, and gives the first read on 2028 hedging.
catalysts.watch: 2027 guide at or above ~$8.1B incl. ~$0.7B Cogentrix+Meta (below $7.4B low end is a thesis hit); 2028 hedge % and price; buyback pace; any new hyperscaler contract; whether guidance waits for the Cogentrix close.

catalysts.event: Cogentrix acquisition close (FERC approved Aug 2026; HSR and customary conditions outstanding)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Unlocks ~5.5 GW of gas and the Cogentrix share of the $0.7B EBITDA add; a slip delays the formal 2027 guide.
catalysts.watch: Closing 8-K; 5M shares issued to seller; $1.5B assumed debt.

catalysts.event: ERCOT files the Batch Zero Eligibility Verification and Community Impact Review reports (governor-ordered data-center audit); energization of new 75 MW+ loads paused until then
catalysts.why_it_moves: Determines how much of the Texas large-load queue is real, which drives the ERCOT load-growth narrative and the 2028 forward curve on VST's open volume.
catalysts.watch: Share of the ~128 GW studied load that survives; restart date for Batch Zero and energizations; any new PUCT rules for large loads or co-location.

catalysts.date: mid-Dec 2026 (agents cite 2026-12-15 close; PJM confirms December)
catalysts.event: PJM 2029/2030 Base Residual Auction under the $325 cap / $175 floor collar
catalysts.why_it_moves: Sets East capacity revenue for June 2029 onward; a fourth cap-level clear supports the out-year story (adds nothing to NTM EBITDA).
catalysts.watch: Clearing price vs $325 cap; reserve shortfall; any talk of extending the collar or more affordability intervention.

catalysts.event: Texas 90th Legislature convenes (session through late May 2027)
catalysts.why_it_moves: Bills on large-load limits, data-center cost allocation or co-location could cut the ERCOT demand story that underpins 2028+ pricing.
catalysts.watch: Filed bills on large-load interconnection, curtailment or co-location; committee hearings in Feb-Mar.

catalysts.event: Q4 2026 results: first 2028 outlook and updated hedge levels (~72% hedged as of Aug 2026)
catalysts.why_it_moves: The 2028 view tells us whether EBITDA grows past 2027 or rolls over as the open ~28% re-hedges at weaker ERCOT forwards; it sets the NTM base at our horizon.
catalysts.watch: 2028 opportunity range vs ~$8.1-8.2B; hedge % and realized prices; buyback authorization.

risks.risk: The Q3 guide lands below the $7.4B low end plus $0.7B, or the 2028 view comes in below 2027, as the ~28% open 2028 volume is re-hedged into weak ERCOT forwards.
risks.signpost: ERCOT 2027/2028 forwards keep falling week over week (they were down ~2.0%/1.7% in the week of Sep 21); management language shifts from 'lower end' to 'below the range'; continued downward EPS revisions.

risks.risk: Texas large-load demand disappoints: the Dec 10 audit culls much of the queue and the 2027 legislature restricts data-center interconnection, cementing the ~$30-34/MWh ERCOT curve.
risks.signpost: Audit reports show a large share of the 128 GW studied load ineligible; Batch Zero restart pushed to late 2027; another EIA STEO cut to Texas load growth (August already cut 2027 to 6% from 14%).

risks.risk: Sector de-rating: IPPs trade as a group on AI-power sentiment and rates; a hyperscaler capex pause or a 10-year above 5% compresses the multiple toward the 7.25x gas-fleet mark (~$105).
risks.signpost: CEG/NRG/TLN falling together with VST; hyperscaler capex guidance cuts; 10-year sustained above 5%.

risks.risk: PJM political intervention: extended or tighter price caps, data-center cost allocation or backstop design that caps East capacity value.
risks.signpost: White House/governor pressure for lower caps, a FERC order changing the collar beyond 2029/30, or the backstop procurement clearing far below cap.

trade.position: 5 sh (~$690, 6.9% of the $10,000 book); binding limit is the supervisor's 7% cap for overlap with the AI-power driver in META/GOOGL
trade.entry: Staged per the supervisor: buy ~3 sh now at ~$138, add the last ~2 sh after the Q3 call (calendars: Nov 5) only if the 2027 guide is at or above ~$8.1B incl. Cogentrix and Meta; hold the second tranche if the guide is below the $7.4B low end or Cogentrix has not closed.
trade.exit_or_add: Exit on a close below $104.94 (the ~$105 thesis break, ~7.2x EBITDA = gas-fleet M&A mark) or on a 2027 guide below $7.4B + $0.7B. Take profit at $206.50 (q75; ~11x, where the Street already is). Add the second tranche on a clean Q3 guide; consider going above the cap only with a new hyperscaler contract or a Dec 10 audit that clears most Batch Zero load. Expected loss at stop ~$165.

what_changes_our_mind: Q3 call guides 2027 below ~$7.9B including Cogentrix and Meta, or signals 2028 below 2027 (bearish: exit).
ERCOT 2028 forwards fall another ~10% into year-end or the Dec 10 audit/2027 legislature materially restricts large loads (bearish: cut).
A new hyperscaler contract (Comanche Peak expansion or a gas-backed PPA) plus a clean audit that reopens Batch Zero (bullish: lift target toward the Street and add above 7%).
